candidates.violated_requirement: Gray-to-binary conversion should use XOR operations to correctly decode the Gray code. Using OR instead of XOR will cause incorrect binary values after the first bit transition, leading to wrong Gray code outputs.
candidates.spec_basis: The Gray code counter should generate a 4-bit Gray code sequence where two successive values differ in only one bit position

candidates.violated_requirement: Binary increment should add 1 to properly sequence through all values. Adding 0 instead will cause the counter to stall at its current value, breaking the Gray code sequence.
candidates.spec_basis: The counter should cycle through all 16 possible 4-bit Gray code values and then repeat

candidates.violated_requirement: Binary-to-Gray conversion requires XOR operations to maintain single-bit transitions. Using AND instead will produce incorrect Gray codes that violate the single-bit change property.
candidates.spec_basis: Gray code is a binary numeral system where two successive values differ in only one bit position

candidates.violated_requirement: Gray-to-binary conversion requires each bit to XOR with the immediately more significant bit. Using bit 2 instead of bit 1 will cause incorrect binary decoding, leading to wrong Gray code outputs.
candidates.spec_basis: The implementation should follow the process of converting Gray code to binary representation correctly
